articles.title_orig: Stock market today: Nasdaq wavers, S&P 500 and Dow climb ahead of Fed decision, Big Tech earnings
articles.title_zh: Stock market today: Nasdaq wavers, S&P 500 and Dow climb ahead of Fed decision, Big Tech earnings
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
US stocks were mixed ahead of a critical day for markets, with a Fed decision and earnings results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) on deck.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) and S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) edged roughly 0.1% higher, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) was slightly below the flatline.
Sentiment in the tech trade has markedly improved this week, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting back-to-back gains. Semiconductor stocks drove the rally on Tuesday after Broadcom's CEO negotiated for a consortium of banks to announce a $63 billion financing structure for building AI compute capacity.
They continued to gain Wednesday after South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix ( SKHY , 000660.KS ) reported that profits grew 632% year over year. Micron ( MU ), Samsung ( 005930.KS ), and other chipmaker stocks also rose.
Attention now turns toward the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision at 2 p.m. ET, where the Fed is expected to hold rates steady despite elevated inflation readings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference will be closely watched for any signs of a hawkish bias. ( Follow live updates from the meeting .)
Earnings season continues apace as two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders — Microsoft and Alphabet — deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the bell. Microsoft's report comes just after it offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees as it tries to streamline operations amid the AI build-out.
Rounding out the earnings picture are Ford ( F ), GE Vernova ( GEV ), T-Mobile US ( TMUS ), eBay ( EBAY ), Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ), and ServiceNow ( NOW ).
Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley reports:
Access to power has emerged as one of the greatest bottlenecks for the AI build-out, with a particular focus on natural gas, which is cheap and abundant in the US.
Anthropic's S-1 filing proves natural gas is "an AI vertical," Melius Research managing director James West said.
"We know power is a constraint to AI and Anthropic's S-1 filing did nothing to assuage that view," West wrote to clients on Tuesday. "AI compute is a natural gas demand story."
Power-intensive data centers are the backbone of the AI build-out. US electricity demand from data centers is expected to double from 2025 to 2027, per research from Goldman Sachs, after 20 years of roughly stagnant energy grid expansion in the US.
US stocks were mixed at Wednesday's open as investors looked ahead to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and earnings from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) was little changed, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed 0.4%.
Tech stocks entered the session with renewed momentum after back-to-back gains for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, while investors awaited fresh signals on AI demand from Microsoft and Alphabet after the bell.
The Fed is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at 2 p.m. ET, with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference closely watched for signs of how willing policymakers are to raise rates again.
Nelson Peltz's Trian Partners has reportedly offered $1.4 billion to buy the struggling fast food giant, according to the Wall Street Journal. Wendy's shares rose 15% in premarket trading on the news.
Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports:
After nearly two years of struggles competing with the likes of behemoths McDonald's ( MCD ) and Yum! Brands' ( YUM ) Taco Bell, plus upstarts such as Shake Shack ( SHAK ), Wendy's is on the cusp of a large number of restaurant closures.
"With one of its largest franchisees filing bankruptcy in September (although contested by WEN given prior termination of franchise agreement), we think investors likely expect closures to tick higher than expected, but we admit visibility on our side remains somewhat limited and there could still be a range of outcomes," veteran restaurant analyst Andy Barish warned in a recent note. "That said, given our view that there are likely additional franchise operators in the system facing challenges with leveraged balance sheets, higher interest rates and profitability pressures from higher beef, labor & build costs (like many others in QSR), we think it is prudent to moderate our development estimates and bake in more potential closures over the next 6-12 months, as the company works to strengthen its system."
Robinhood ( HOOD ) warned Wednesday that its new artificial intelligence agents could execute unintended trades and expose the online trading platform to new regulatory and legal risks.
Robinhood opened its platform to AI agents brought by customers in May, and began rolling out an in-app version last month . The company warned in its third-quarter regulatory filing that the expansion creates "greater reputational risk" as the technology reaches more investors.
In an interview last month, Robinhood said customers are responsible for trades executed by their agents. But the company now acknowledges that courts or regulators might not uphold its customer agreements that assign responsibility to its customers.
The new warnings were added in the risk factor section of the company's 10-Q filing. Robinhood shares fell nearly 8% in Wednesday premarket trading after it reported weaker-than-expected third quarter profits Tuesday.
US-listed shares of SK Hynix ( SKHY ) rose 8% in premarket trading on Wednesday, after the memory maker's record profit and revenue quelled recent investor worries over the AI trade.
South Korean SK Hynix shares ( 000660.KS ) jumped 10% while peer Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) gained 5%. US-based Micron ( MU ) also rose 2%.
The South Korea-based company reported a 328% jump in quarterly revenue to roughly $78.7 billion, while operating profit surged 632% to about $62.7 billion, delivering an 80% operating margin. Revenue and operating profit increased by 32% and 38%, respectively, from the previous quarter.
Growth was driven by surging AI data center demand, higher memory prices, and early shipments of HBM4, which SK Hynix expects to replace HBM3E as its mainstream product.
Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger previews what to expect and look for in the Federal Reserve's policy announcement and press conference on Wednesday afternoon:
The Federal Reserve heads into its interest-rate decision this week facing hotter inflation, keeping the meeting live even as markets widely expect the central bank to hold interest rates steady just days before the midterm elections.
Alan Blinder, a former Fed vice chair and a Princeton University economics professor, is expecting a "hawkish pause."
Although Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh doesn't favor telegraphing the central bank's next move, Blinder said the moment calls for clarity.
"This is a perfect time for clear forward guidance that doesn't quite say, but strongly hints, we're pausing now, but we stand ready to raise again and even give a hint that the next meeting might be the next interest rate hike."
Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre writes:
The stock market's favorite season starts Monday. For decades, November through April has beaten the rest of the year by a mile.
That's the Halloween indicator , also called the "best six months" or "sell in May." Buy stocks at the end of October, hold them through April, then step aside for the summer.
Yale Hirsch found the pattern in 1986. "You can divide the year into two sections and have practically all the gains in one six-month section and very little in the other," his son Jeffrey Hirsch, editor in chief of the Stock Trader's Almanac, wrote in the 2026 edition.
Since 1950, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) has gained an average of about 7% from November through April, versus less than 1% from May through October, according to the Stock Trader's Almanac. Put $10,000 into only the good half each year, and it grew to about $1.3 million. Put it into only the bad half, and it shrank to about $4,300.

Israel ’s election has ended in a deadlock as no party is on track for a majority of the Knesset , exit polls have suggested.
The stalemate comes after three years of war waged in Gaza , Lebanon and Iran , which have plunged the Middle East into turmoil.
The election is widely seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu , who is seeking another term after a combined 19 years in power .
But now, the jostling for power between parties to achieve a governing coalition and name the next prime minister could take weeks or even months.
There are 38 different parties contesting the election, but most will not get enough votes to secure one of the 120 seats in the Knesset.
Israeli elections are based on nationwide proportional representation. Citizens cast votes for a single party – not for individual candidates – and the party’s number of seats is determined by the proportion of the national vote it receives.
To actually enter the Knesset, a party must receive at least 3.25 per cent of the vote, or four seats.
Historically, no single party has won a majority, ​so governments are formed by a coalition. If no one manages to form a coalition with a 61-seat majority, citizens return to the ballot box.
Polls opened at 7am local time and closed at 10pm that night (8pm GMT). An exit poll by Israeli TV channels revealed the initial results, but the official, full results will not be confirmed until Tuesday 4 November.
However, the whole process will take much longer, ranging from 20 to 100 days. In the past two decades, no government has been sworn in in less than 50 days.
After a coalition agreement is signed, the Knesset convenes a special session during which the designated prime minister presents the new government and its policy agenda.
A formal vote is then held, and if the new government wins the vote, it starts its tenure.
The election is viewed domestically as one of the most consequential in the history of Israel .
The outcome could have profound consequences for Palestinians and Israel’s relations with neighbouring states, as well as international partners like the US and Europe.
Some of the main issues centre on the debate over exemptions from military service for ultra-Orthodox Jews , how the state should investigate its inability to prevent the October 7 2023 Hamas attacks and future concessions in Gaza , the occupied West Bank and Lebanon.
Israel’s wars have also put pressure on the economy, so the cost of living will definitely weigh on people’s minds when casting their votes. For context, the state’s defence budget has doubled since 2023.
Two main blocs – of nearly equal weight – are facing off against each other. One is an alliance of far-right parties dominated by Netanyahu, and the other camp is led by Yashar’s Gadi Eisenkot, a former head of the Israel Defence Forces.
The current exit polls released by major Israeli TV stations suggested that Netanyahu’s bloc won 50 seats, the opposition won 52-53 and Arab parties won 17-18.
Dr Nimrod Nir, of Agam Labs, said that “the real political drama will begin the morning after the election”.
“Israel’s election is not a single game, but a tournament – and election day is only the opening round,” he added.
“Our polling suggests that neither bloc is likely to secure a governing majority, leaving three possible outcomes: a unity government bringing Netanyahu together with more liberal parties, an alternative coalition backed by Arab parties, or yet another election.”

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.content_orig:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on Wednesday that any Israeli-instigated attack in the Gulf region would have a "devastating impact" on global markets.
"Devastating impact on int'l markets of any Israel-instigated military misadventure in Persian Gulf region remains major concern for both gas suppliers and consumers," Araghchi said in a post on X .
The United States and Israel have in recent days raised the prospect of renewed attacks on Iran in the war, which began in late February with strikes on the Islamic republic.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is seeking to form a new government after close elections, said on Wednesday he could work with President Trump to eliminate the "existential threat" posed by Iran.
Iran's Embassy in Kuwait has categorically rejected the Kuwaiti government's allegation that an Iranian citizen was involved in a plot to assassinate public figures or in any other activity that could undermine Kuwait's national security.
The embassy said in a statement that it "categorically rejects the allegation made by the Kuwaiti government regarding the involvement of an Iranian citizen in a plot to assassinate public figures or in any other act that could undermine Kuwait's national security, and recalls that the aforementioned individual has not been present in Kuwait at any time during the past ten years."
A Kuwaiti State Security and Terrorism Criminal Court sentenced three men to death on Monday over an alleged plot to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef, with prosecutors accusing the defendants of spying for Iran, communicating with Iranian-linked entities and joining Hezbollah, two judicial sources told the AFP news agency Tuesday.
The court also sentenced eight other defendants to varying prison terms.
According to Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Rai , the defendants were accused of communicating with Iran and entities allegedly operating in its interests, including Lebanese group Hezbollah, to carry out hostile acts against Kuwait following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on Feb. 28, at the beginning of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels said Wednesday Saudi Arabia killed dozens of people with strikes in Yemen. The group also said it had targeted the perimeter of an airport in government-held Aden
Houthi broadcaster Almasirah reported 14 dead "and 10 wounded, including women and children in a preliminary toll," in attacks blamed on Saudi Arabia that hit a market and a petrol station in the northwestern Jawf province.
In Aden, a Houthi missile fell inside the perimeter of the airport shortly before the Iran-backed group issued a call to evacuate the area, a local police source told the AFP news agency.
The source added that the strike hit while a Saudi military aircraft was at the airport, but the plane "was not hit and took off shortly afterward."
He spoke on condition of anonymity due to security concerns.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on Telegram that the cargo plan was "transporting weapons to kill the sons of the Yemeni people."
The Houthis have targeted Aden several times in recent weeks. They have also intensified attacks on their Saudi foe, while they battle the government it backs in Aden.
The United States has told its Gulf allies to prepare for a brief but intense campaign against Iran after the midterm elections, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people briefed on the matter.
The U.S. military is shipping a Patriot antimissile system from Texas to Israel and has transferred troops off bases where they may have been vulnerable, officials familiar with the decisions told the outlet.
American forces across the Middle East have been restocking munitions and aircraft have been preparing for strikes, the paper reported, while an additional aircraft carrier strike group and Marine unit are set to join the 20 or so warships in the region, though some other vessels could be withdrawn.
The Houthis have called on people in Aden International Airport in southern Yemen to evacuate immediately, claiming that a Saudi military cargo aircraft is transporting weapons there intended to kill Yemenis.
Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said in a post on X : "Our armed forces call on those present at Aden Airport to evacuate the airport immediately, due to the presence of an enemy Saudi military cargo aircraft transporting weapons to kill the sons of the Yemeni people."
Aden is the seat of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, and has been since the Iran-backed Houthis took the country's capital, Sanaa, in 2014.
A senior Iranian official denied Wednesday that Qatar had presented Tehran with a new peace proposal, saying instead that Qatar had come with "unacceptable" ideas, the Reuters news agency reported.
Reuters reported earlier Wednesday that Qatari mediators handed Iran a new draft deal to end the war on Sunday, citing an official briefed on the negotiations.
Dismissing the idea that they had been given a new peace proposal, the Iranian official speaking to the news agency said Tehran would show no flexibility on the nuclear issue.
Qatari mediators on Sunday handed Iran a new draft deal to end the war, the Reuters news agency reported, citing an official briefed on the negotiations.
Tehran is considering the proposal and set to respond by the end of the week, the agency reported Wednesday.
The source added that there were concerns in Tehran before the meeting on Sunday that Israel could resume its bombardment of Iran this week.
The cost of the Iran war has risen to an estimated $47 billion, according to an estimate from the U.S. military's Central Command obtained by CBS News Tuesday.
Like previous estimates, it does not include damage to U.S. military bases in the Middle East. The bulk of the cost, $29 billion, is for replacing expended munitions.
According to a report released by the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office in September, the Iran war could cost approximately $2 billion to $3 billion per month for as long as it continues.
Exit polls from Israel's major television networks project that a majority of Israelis voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition in Tuesday's election, but his Likud party still emerged as the largest party among all the contenders. Neither bloc, Netanyahu or the opposition, has a clear majority.
While Netanyahu appears to have won fewer votes than his main challenger, according to the early exit polls, both candidates will likely struggle to cobble together a coalition.
One or the other would need to obtain majority support in Israel's 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset, in order to form a government.
Israel's two Arab parties won more seats in parliament than in any previous election. That electoral success comes after what some Arab voters told CBS News was a difficult time for them in the country under the hard-right government of Netanyahu, prompting a historic turnout for the minority community.
Both Netanyahu and those opposing him have vowed not to form a government reliant on Arab parties, arguing it would endanger the country if they gain enough seats to influence Israel's engagement in its myriad conflicts. Arab citizens of Israel are around 20% of the population.

articles.title_orig: America's largest budget airline reports 71% jump in airfare
articles.title_zh: America's largest budget airline reports 71% jump in airfare
articles.content_orig:
Frontier Airlines reported a 71% increase in airfare in the third quarter as the country's largest budget airline tried to pass along an even bigger jump in jet fuel prices.
Frontier's fare revenue averaged $67.82 per passenger in the third quarter, compared with $39.74 last year. Including the budget airline's many fees, such as for checked and carry-on luggage, total revenue per passenger rose 30% on the year to $138.22.
Customers kept booking despite the higher prices. Frontier's passenger count rose 18% to more than 9.8 million people in the quarter. That's a difference of 1.5 million passengers from last year.
The company said demand remains strong, even at these higher prices, but Frontier still lost money. The airline widened its third-quarter loss to $104 million from a $77 million loss a year earlier. Its fuel bill soared 82% to $425 million.
Frontier forecast potential adjusted profit in the fourth quarter, saying it expects to post an adjusted loss of 15 cents per share to adjusted earnings of as much as 5 cents per share.
Carriers from Delta Air Lines to Frontier have said customers are mostly continuing to book flights despite higher fares, but that record jet fuel prices, their biggest cost after labor, are eroding profits.
Frontier shares were up about 6% in early trading Wednesday.
Frontier had eclipsed Spirit Airlines as the biggest discount carrier in the country even before that airline collapsed in May.

articles.title_orig: Hansell learns about healthcare firsthand in China
articles.title_zh: Hansell learns about healthcare firsthand in China
articles.content_orig:
By Terry Murry on Wednesday, October 28th, 2026 in Columbia Basin News Columbia Basin Top Stories
ATHENA – Retired Oregon Senator Bill Hansell went to China for two weeks as a tourist and a speaker at the Oregon China Council gathering in Tianjin on Oct. 11. He, his wife Margaret, and son Bill went to the Great Wall of China on their first day and then took a bullet train to Tianjin.
That’s when everything changed.
“Coming out of a toilet stall at Tianjin University of Technology, I failed to negotiate a six-inch step and had – as I can best describe – an epic crash to the bathroom floor, knocking myself out which opened a gash on the back of my head,” he wrote.
He regained consciousness in a hospital, suffering from a concussion and a brain bleed. His son Bill presented the paper he was to deliver. Meanwhile, Hansell says he got to experience outstanding medical care.
“Compassion, kindness, and concern were combined with state-of-the-art medical procedures to help me get back on my feet,” he said.
As is the custom in China, a bed was moved into his room so Margaret Hansell could sleep there. After three days in the hospital he went to Beijing for two days of more medical tests and received clearance to fly home.
“Our Chinese hosts took great care of us in Tianjin and Beijing,” Hansell wrote on Facebook. “They made sure we had transportation and interpreters for all our medical appointments.”
Hansell said that he, Margaret, and son Bill definitely experienced a proverb that they hold close. Proverbs 16:9: “The mind of man plans his way, but the Lord directs his steps.”
When his steps brought him home to Athena, he found out he was something of a celebrity in China. China Daily , the official American-language newspaper of the Chinese government, had published a story about his stay.
Hansell told the Chinese reporter that he hopes to return to China because the experience has “built a bridge that is very strong.”
He also expressed his gratitude to China to us.
“I will forever have a special place in my heart for everyone who took care of this Oregon farm boy,” Hansell said.
The China Daily article is at Former Oregon state senator’s Tianjin fall becomes story of unexpected kindness – Chinadaily.com.cn .

articles.title_orig: Mercedes-Benz to Offer Voluntary Buyouts for Support Staff as Market Worsens
articles.title_zh: Mercedes-Benz to Offer Voluntary Buyouts for Support Staff as Market Worsens
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Mercedes-Benz on Tuesday became the third big German carmaker to cut its outlook for the year on tough conditions in China, underlining the scale of the crisis facing the industry.
Citing difficulties in China -- the world's largest car market -- as well as higher material costs, core profit for 2026 is now expected to be on a par with the prior year's 5.8 billion euros ($6.5 billion), the company said.
It had previously foreseen an increase of at least 15 percent.
Profit margins at the core car business are now indicated at between two and three percent for the year, Mercedes-Benz said, down from the three to five percent previously.
Mercedes-Benz shares fell 4.2 percent after the cut. Volkswagen and BMW were both down a little over two percent.
BMW and Volkswagen have both already cut their guidance for the year as sluggish demand combined with cut-throat competition from Chinese local rivals such as BYD and Xiaomi have eaten into profits.
Mercedes-Benz's vehicle deliveries in China -- last year already at their lowest level since 2016 -- fell a further 29 percent in the nine months to end-September.
Being partially muscled out of China has led to painful adjustments for Germany's car industry, one of the country's largest employers.
Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kaellenius has urged German workers to work extra hours without pay at the same time as expanding the company's manufacturing footprint in Hungary, where he says costs are about 70 percent lower than in Germany.
Volkswagen plans to have cut 120,000 jobs globally by the end of the decade in what is the largest restructuring in automotive history, eclipsing the 50,000 jobs lost after the bankruptcy of General Motors in 2009.
Core profit for the third quarter came in at 1.77 billion euros, Mercedes-Benz said in preliminary results, and the profit margin at the cars business was 2.5 percent.
"Structural challenges show no sign of abating," Ingo Speich, head of sustainability and corporate governance at Mercedes-Benz shareholder Deka Investment, told AFP.
"The poor results highlight just how essential further cost-cutting measures –- as well as attractive new products –- are. Both must be implemented sooner rather than later."
Mercedes-Benz reports full third-quarter results on Wednesday.

articles.content_orig:

An ​attacker with two knives who wounded a policeman guarding the Israeli embassy in Belgrade overnight has been shot dead.
Serbia's outgoing interior minister confirmed the news on Wednesday.
“One minor, of so far undetermined identity, who is reasonably suspected to be from Šabac, ⁠rushed at an ​officer of the ⁠Gendarmerie shouting ‘Allahu Akbar’ and attacked him with two knives,” Ivica Dacic ⁠said in an emailed statement.
Dacic added that ​he ⁠had raised Serbia's ‌security threat level to red, the highest, and that there would be an increased police ‌presence at key locations. ‌The officer suffered a light head wound, Dacic said.
It is the second such attack at Belgrade's ⁠Israeli embassy in two years. In June 2024, an assailant shot a Serbian police officer with a crossbow.
The attack came a day after Israelis went to the polls, with projected results showing the ‌opposition bloc neck and neck ​with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp.
Israel's Central Elections Committee was tallying votes on Wednesday and it will likely take until Thursday before definitive results of the election - the first since the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023 - are known.
With some 48.4% of votes tallied, Netanyahu's bloc was projected to ⁠win 55 seats, and Eisenkot's bloc 50 seats, with 15 seats going to Arab parties, Israeli media reported, a distribution will likely change as more votes are tallied.
That leaves both sides short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, and neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot claimed victory.
Serbia's ‌student-led movement toppled longtime ⁠leader Aleksandar Vucic in an election ⁠on Sunday, but the outgoing administration remains in place ‌in a ​caretaker role until the new ‌government is formed.
Protesters entered a Serbian television station supportive of Vucic late on Monday, interrupting broadcasting to call for the arrest of its editor, as tens of thousands took to the streets for ⁠a second night of post-election celebrations.
Serbia's Student List, born out of a student-led anti-corruption protest movement, unseated Vucic in a historic election, bringing to an end 14 years in power for a man who served as information minister under Slobodan Milosevic and who maintained tight control over the media.
Live footage broadcast by Informer TV showed around 30 people walk ⁠into its newsroom on Monday evening and surround editor-in-chief and owner ​Dragan ⁠Vucicevic. Some protesters shouted: "This is how it is in free Serbia" and "Where is Vucic now?" Some also called for Vucicevic's arrest.
On his personal Instagram account, Vucic, dressed in a jumper displaying the ⁠crossed-out word "sorry", called the event an attack on free speech and the freedom of journalism.

articles.title_orig: Houthis strike Yemen's Aden airport after evacuation warning
articles.title_zh: Houthis strike Yemen's Aden airport after evacuation warning
articles.content_orig:
Houthi fighters have launched a series of attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia and the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised government in Aden, while the fighting intensifies around the city of Taiz.
In a Facebook post on Saturday, the Yemeni government’s Ministry of Transport denounced what it described as the Houthis’ targeting of Aden international airport with two ballistic missiles, calling it the “fourth such attack this month”.
The airport attacks pose “a threat to the safety of civil aviation” and have “humanitarian and economic repercussions for citizens” who rely on it, the ministry warned.
Yemeni authorities said the coastguard headquarters and a second building were also hit.
The Houthis claimed attacks on the al-Nasr camp and Aden’s naval military base.
Yemen’s army said a Houthi missile killed three people when it malfunctioned and fell on a family home in Houthi-held Sanaa on Friday. The army said it was one of several missile malfunctions seen in recent weeks by the Iran-backed group.
Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said on Saturday that Saudi-led coalition air attacks killed several civilians in the capital, Sanaa, and in the port city of Hodeidah. The claim could not be verified and Saudi Arabia has not commented on the alleged raids.
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Sunday that it downed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital, Riyadh.
“Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh,” the coalition’s spokesperson said in a social media post.
On Saturday, Saudi Arabia’s civil defence said on X the Houthis had launched two ballistic missiles towards Mecca and Medina, warning of “the fall of shrapnel” following their interception.
Images shared on X by the Saudi Press Agency appeared to show a large, blackened missile-shaped object that had landed somewhere in Saudi Arabia.
Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, secretary-general of the Gulf Cooperation Council, described the Houthi attacks as “heinous” and said they embodied “a blatant disregard for the lives and security of civilians” in a statement shared on Saturday.
The Houthis said the claim that they targeted the two cities – the holiest in Islam – was a “huge lie”. They said their targets were three Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and an airbase.
The Houthis have persistently targeted Saudi energy infrastructure and airports across the country with long-range strikes since a fragile ceasefire agreed in 2022 fell apart in July .
Riyadh’s international airport said in a social media post on Saturday that flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following Houthi strikes on the capital.
Shortly after the announcement, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree issued a warning on X, saying the airport is still “unsafe” and remains a “military target”.
The Flightradar24 monitoring site showed a plane taking off from Riyadh airport early on Sunday, heading to the Saudi city of Jeddah.
Intense fighting is continuing on Yemen’s front lines as the Houthis battle forces of the internationally recognised government for control of key areas.
On Saturday, Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said government forces had carried out more than 700 “targeting operations” over the last 24 hours across Yemen, “neutralising” 300 Houthi fighters and disabling military vehicles.
Al Jazeera could not independently verify those figures.
Operations targeted field command centres, Houthi gatherings, weapons depots, and supply lines in Taiz, where intense clashes have been ongoing for days, the spokesman added.
The Houthis have been launching attacks on the western, eastern and southern fronts of Taiz, with attempts by Houthi fighters to break through and advance from the western front towards the city of Taiz in an effort to capture it, Al Jazeera correspondent Hadeel al-Yamani reported on Saturday.
Government forces, supported by fighters from the Popular Resistance group, have pushed back against Houthi attacks to break through from the eastern front.

articles.title_orig: Exclusive | Nelson Peltz’s Trian Offers to Buy Wendy’s for $1.4 Billion
articles.title_zh: Exclusive | Nelson Peltz’s Trian Offers to Buy Wendy’s for $1.4 Billion
articles.content_orig:
A group of investors led by Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management has offered $1.4 billion to buy Wendy's , according to a regulatory filing Wednesday.
The group has offered $7.35 per share in cash to take the burger chain private, paying a 20% premium to Tuesday's closing price. In addition to Trian, it includes investment firms BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners, plus Flynn Group, one of Wendy's largest franchisees.
Wendy's shares spiked about 15% in morning trading following the offer. The Wall Street Journal first reported Peltz's proposal.
Wendy's did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC. Trian declined to comment beyond the filing.
The take-private deal offer comes after a tough two-year stretch for the burger chain. Wendy's stock has tumbled 65% over that period, including Wednesday's gains. For six straight quarters, the company has reported same-store sales declines.
Wendy's is scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings before the bell on Nov. 5.
Wendy's challenges have made the company a cheaper acquisition target for Peltz, whose history with the brand dates back to an activist campaign he led more than two decades ago.
Budget-conscious diners have been eating out less often, and Wendy's and its rivals have leaned into discounts to lure consumers into restaurants. Wendy's has also dealt with a revolving door of chief executives, who have had different ideas about turnaround strategies for the struggling chain.
In May, former Potbelly CEO Bob Wright joined Wendy's as its latest chief executive, after his former employer went private. In his first earnings conference call with analysts in August, he was candid about what he views as the chain's biggest issues, like muddled value offerings, inconsistent execution at its restaurants and too many one-off promotions.
Trian previously explored a takeover of Wendy's in 2022, but later decided against it. The firm and affiliated parties own a 16.25% stake in Wendy's, according to the regulatory filing.

articles.title_orig: Pip payment denied for terminally ill mum with cancer
articles.title_zh: Pip payment denied for terminally ill mum with cancer
articles.content_orig:
A terminally ill mum who has been given three years to live has been denied disability benefit despite being unable to eat, talk, dress or use the toilet independently.
Rachael Field, 56, from Rhondda Cynon Taf, who has tongue cancer, was first diagnosed six years ago.
She uses a feeding tube, has had her tongue and voice box removed, and had her windpipe reconstructed using chest tissue. Field also has mobility issues.
Earlier this year, she was denied Personal Independence Payment (Pip), to support people with disability-related extra costs.
The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) said it needed further evidence to complete the claim and was sorry for "any distress" to the family.
Field said she has had cancer four times in six years, and now cannot do anything for herself.
"I need help to wash, dress and use the bathroom. I can only walk a few steps with help. I cannot eat or drink, everything has to go through my feeding tube," she added.
The former factory worker was forced to stop working following her terminal diagnosis, and her family has been managing the financial strain.
Field applied for Pip in May, but it was denied as she was awarded zero points across all assessed categories.
Pip is a benefit people with long-term illnesses and disabilities can claim if they need help with extra costs associated with living, work and care. Eligibility is determined through an assessment.
Under the current system, claimants are scored on a zero to 12 scale by a health professional on everyday tasks such as washing, getting dressed and preparing food.
Field's family said repeated rescheduling of the assessment process caused delays, and that despite lodging an appeal several months ago, they are still awaiting an outcome.
Field said the treatment she received from her medical test "has been outstanding" but has an issue with "the system Pip uses to assess people".
She said: "People need the help while they are alive."
Her daughter, Kyra Hawkins-Field, 20, said it is "ridiculous" that her mum has not been able to claim Pip and does not want her "stressing about money" while she only has "a couple of years left".
She criticised the benefits assessment process and said it was too reliant on a checklist, and did not reflect people's real-life struggles.
"They've basically turned around and said, 'we think you're fine'," she said.
Hawkins-Field said her dad Eddie has become the family's "superhero", working full-time and then visiting his wife in hospital every day.
The couple married 15 years ago after meeting when they both worked in a factory. They enjoy visiting towns across Wales, and still hope to visit Scotland and Ireland one day.
Hawkins-Field said her mum likes the "little things in life", but "loves doing jigsaw puzzles, big, really, really difficult, intricate jigsaw puzzles" and reading.
Hawkins-Field launched a GoFundMe appeal with the aim of raising £1,000 to help her mum enjoy what time she has left with her family, including some trips around the UK, while she still can.
A DWP spokesperson said: "We're sorry for any distress Ms Field and her family are feeling at this difficult time.
"We have been unable to complete the claim as we need further evidence from Ms Field. We have attempted to contact her in order to resolve the situation and will continue to do so."
Field's family said they were in discussion with the DWP.

articles.title_orig: Amazon Debuts 16-Inch Echo Smart Display and Alexa Photo Frame
articles.title_zh: Amazon Debuts 16-Inch Echo Smart Display and Alexa Photo Frame
articles.content_orig:
Along with speaker and Echo Show upgrades, Amazon unveiled a smart alarm clock and photo frame.
Apple isn't the only major tech company announcing new devices this week . Amazon has a bunch of new and updated products to show off as well. The company has been dripfeeding its reveals over the last several weeks , and now it's announcing its latest Echo devices.
Along with updated Echo speakers and a revamped Echo Show 16, there are some brand new devices in the mix. Echo Time is a smart alarm clock, while the Alexa Smart Frame is a way for you to show off family photos (and ask questions to an AI assistant, if you want). The company also has a new Echo Studio speaker with a camera.
Here's a peek at all the Echo devices Amazon announced today.
Amazon says it refreshed the Echo Dot with an upgraded speaker. There's an extra beamform microphone, which brings the total in the device to four, while the company says it updated the noise reduction algorithm, so the speaker should be able to more easily understand your Alexa commands.
The Echo Dot now has an AZ3 chip that's said to allow for "faster, more natural conversations with Alexa+." Voice ID can recognize the user for personalized features like access to their own playlists.
This speaker can function as a smart home hub, with support for devices that use the Zigbee, Thread and Matter standards. In addition, it can act as a Wi-Fi extender for Eero routers.
The new Echo Dot is available today. It comes in one of four colors (graphite, glacier white, agave green and coral pink) and it costs $99. A kids version comes with a year of access to Kids+ and Sleep Studio services like Calm. This model (which is available in designs called octopus and penguin) costs $110.
There's a fresh version of another of Amazon's speakers, the Echo Studio. This new model has a camera built in. Amazon says the camera won't record footage. Instead, it acts as a way for you to get a live view of what's going on in your home, such as to see what your pets are up to while you're out.
The camera supports face recognition, which is used for personalization (in similar fashion to Apple's HomeView ). There's Voice ID support as well. You can also access Alexa+ visual intelligence features and ask the assistant questions based on what the camera can see.
Perhaps the most interesting thing about the camera is that it can help tune audio through a feature called Advanced Room Adaptation. It uses Omnisense to detect how many people are in the space then adapt the audio for them and the acoustics of the room. The tool can also automatically adjust the volume based on where you are at a given moment.
Moreover, the Echo Studio with Camera can be used as part of an Alexa Home Theater system. The device costs $250 and an optional stand is $40. The regular Echo Studio remains available.
Next up is something new, the Alexa Photo Frame . As you might imagine, this is a smart picture frame. Amazon says it designed this to be subtle and look like a normal photo frame.
The device is integrated with Amazon Photos, which has unlimited storage for Prime subscribers. It has a 10-inch touch display and built-in Alexa+. You can, for instance, ask Alexa to look at several photos of someone and pick the best ones to send to the photo frame and feature. You can add voice notes to photos too.
The Alexa Photo Frame starts at $200 for a model with a black frame. If you'd prefer one with a real birch or walnut frame, you'll need to fork over $229.
Also new is Echo Time , a device that has zero chance of replacing my beloved Alarmo . It's a smart alarm clock that's supposed to help folks sleep better via an array of wind-down and wake-up features.
Amazon says Echo Time has an ultrasonic transducer that can detect when you're sleeping. It uses light to help wake you up on a schedule that's attuned to your circadian rhythm. So, if you tell Alexa+ you need to be awake by a certain time, the clock can detect when you're in a lighter part of your sleep cycle and start rousing you then (anywhere between 10 and 60 minutes before you've gotta get up). There are a range of alarm tones to choose from too.
There's no camera in the Echo Time, which has hundreds of clock faces available. The 2.3-inch, circular screen can drop to under 0.3 nits of brightness, so it shouldn't disturb you at night.
Echo Time is available today and it costs $199. The color options are graphite, glacier white and coral pink.
A kids version includes Sleep Studio, a year of Kids+ access and different clock face options. It's available in grape and cosmic lime designs, and it costs $210. Parents can manage their kid's Echo Time.
Last but not least is the latest Echo Show. The Echo Show 16 is said to be 40 percent thinner with bezels that are 80 percent thinner than previous models. Amazon says there's a Nanomatte option available for the 16-inch display. This features the same anti-glare tech it used for the Amazon Alexa Tablet Pro 12.
There are several Screen Styles you can switch between, namely a family organizer, photo frame, Fire TV interface and a smart home hub. The latter includes a new feature called Alexa Home Map . It can use cameras to map your house and show where various devices are, which could help you control and manage smart home devices. Omnisense tech can detect when you enter the room and adjust things like the thermostat automatically.
The device will organize all of your Alexa conversations into cards to help you revisit topics that you've discussed with the assistant. These are arranged by topic and you can pin cards for easy access. These are also available on the Alexa app and website.
On the audio front, the Echo Show 16 boasts four beamform microphones, eight woofers and two tweeters. Amazon says the 13MP camera is the most advanced one it's ever included in this product line — it can seemingly recognize users from up to 17 feet away. This is the first Echo Show with night vision support too. There's a button that can disable the camera and mics.
Pre-orders for the Echo Show 16 open today and the device will ship by the end of the year. The standard model costs $500 and one with a Nanomatte display will run you $570. If you pre-order an Echo Show 16, you'll get a $100 discount.
The Echo Show 16 is primarily designed to be hung on walls, though you can snap up a regular stand for $70. A stand that can tilt and swivel costs $125.

articles.title_orig: The Alexa Home Map Is A Visual Way To See And Control Your Smart Home
articles.title_zh: The Alexa Home Map Is A Visual Way To See And Control Your Smart Home
articles.content_orig:
In case you're sick of remembering what you named your thirteenth lamp.
Alongside a slew of Echo devices, Amazon also introduced a new smart home interface today. It's called the Alexa Home Map, and the company describes it as "an interactive 3D map that lets you see and control your home."
Most modern control panels from the likes of Google and Apple display your collection of connected home devices as tiles on a page. You open an app, whether it's Google Home or Apple Home, and you're presented with rows and columns of these cards. Depending on the type of device represented, you can either tap on a card to turn a light on, or drag a slider on it to adjust things like volume or brightness. But this setup requires you to either scroll through a list of rooms in your home or sort by type of device or pin your most commonly used items to the dashboard.
It's something we've gotten used to, but is not necessarily the most intuitive. With the Alexa Home Map, you can get a digital blueprint of your home, and it will feature animated icons for things you can control. Light bulbs and speakers appear on the map where they're located, which is handy if you've forgotten what you've named a specific fixture and only remember where they're placed.
The Alexa Home Map also works with outdoor security cameras to show you what's around your house, including passing vehicles and pedestrians. But rather than present photorealistic representations of individuals, the map uses a visualization that to me was initially reminiscent of scenes from The Sims . I almost expected some of the faux people to randomly spasm like my Sims characters. I later found out that the visual identity was more inspired by the likes of Tesla's Driving Visualization, which made sense.
According to Amazon, the map "updates dynamically in real time, showing the colorful glow of your smart lights and animations of cars and people moving around your yard." In a demo I saw at the company's briefing event this week, the Home Map even showed precipitation like snow and rain, when it was reflective of the local weather.
The company added that lights on the map will glow "in the same color and brightness they're set to, so a blue-lit living room or a dimmed bedroom looks that way on screen." A speaker that's actively playing will show music notes dancing around it. "These touches make the map feel less like a diagram and more like a living picture of your home, and it'll continue to get even better over time," Amazon said in its press release.
To set up your Alexa Home Map when it's available later this year, you'll start by entering your address. Amazon says "the exterior of your home appears automatically" once you do. Then, you'll have to take your compatible iPhone (or Android when it rolls out there) and walk through your home to scan the interior. This uses LIDAR, so it's likely that there won't be a lot of non-iPhone devices that will be compatible with it.
Once you're done with the scan, you'll need to "place your devices on the map right where they sit in your home." I can't tell how involved this process is – I can only imagine that sitting down and drawing up where all 120 of the lights in your massive mansion would take hours. But that's probably a problem that someone that can afford a mansion would not deign to worry about.
Amazon said that "once your map is built, you can move around it however you like, zooming into individual rooms and switching between floors." You can also filter out the devices you're seeing on the map by their type, so you can quickly get a view of just the lights or plugs in your home. You can also use light mode or dark mode, depending on your preferences.
Alexa Home Map "will start to roll out in preview later this year on the Alexa Home Map app on iOS," and it'll also arrive on the Alexa and Ring apps. In addition, larger Echo Show devices like the Ember Artline Fire TV, as well as the new Alexa Tablets and Echo Show 16. A spokesperson at the event told me that Android support will be coming in early 2027.

articles.content_orig:

If you get Global News from Instagram or Facebook - that will be changing. Find out how you can still connect with us .
The Bank of Canada hiked interest rates by 0.25 per cent on Wednesday to 2.5 per cent, marking the first change to its benchmark in a year and the first increase in three years.
The move was widely expected by most economists as the central bank faces pressure to raise interest rates with the Iran war and other geopolitical conflicts resulting in higher prices for oil and gas, which is expected to lead to higher prices for goods and services beyond the gas pump.
Consumer inflation was last measured at 3.1 per cent in September , and has been hovering around three per cent since April.
The Bank of Canada said in a statement it expects inflation to rise to about 3.5 per cent by the end of the year, as oil and gas prices push up the headline figure. When stripping away elevated gasoline prices, core measures of inflation have been closer to two per cent — the Bank’s target — but that is expected to change.
“Cost pressures are building, with high fuel prices raising the costs of production and transportation. Imported industrial and electronics input prices have also increased,” the Bank of Canada said.
“While businesses have mostly absorbed higher input costs so far, Bank surveys suggest cost pass-through will increase over the next year. Near-term household and business inflation expectations have risen, while longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored.”
The Bank adds that its outlook for inflation is higher than its projections from July.
Financial markets and a Reuters poll of economists were betting that the central bank would deliver a quarter-point hike to its policy rate, the first increase in the key lending rate since July 2023.
The floor for borrowing rates set by the Bank of Canada was at 2.25 per cent since October 2025, when rates were cut from 2.5 per cent.
The Bank of Canada also released its updated forecasts for inflation and economic growth Wednesday, and said higher oil and gas prices are expected to continue accelerating inflation.
“With persistently elevated oil prices and refinery margins, inflation has risen in most countries,” said the Bank of Canada in a statement.
“The conflict in the Middle East is now in its eighth month and there is no clear path to resolution. The combination of higher-for-longer energy prices and increased pass-through adds to the persistence of inflation.”
The Bank of Canada said it expects the Canadian economy to grow in total by one per cent this year, and two per cent in 2027 and 2028 respectively, but stressed its forecast is “subject to considerable uncertainty,” especially because of trade tensions between Canada and the U.S.
Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem is scheduled to speak at 10:30 a.m. Eastern time.

articles.title_orig: They bought cabins to live on a luxury cruise ship. High fuel costs got them kicked off in Cambodia.
articles.title_zh: They bought cabins to live on a luxury cruise ship. High fuel costs got them kicked off in Cambodia.
articles.content_orig:
A residential cruise ship halted operations in Cambodia on Tuesday amid soaring fuel costs , leaving passengers in limbo after the U.S. company that operates it ordered them to disembark.
Florida-based Villa Vie Residences said in a news release that it was working to identify “temporary living arrangements” for people aboard The Odyssey, a 642-foot cruise ship that launched from Belfast, Northern Ireland, three years ago and promised passengers “an unparalleled lifestyle of luxury and exploration” as it toured the planet.
Cabins on The Odyssey were for sale or rent.
According to the company , the ship can accommodate 650 residents. A Cambodian official said Wednesday there were 203 passengers and 156 ​crew members on the ship. Some passengers had already departed on ​flights, while others were waiting in the port city of Sihanoukville, Long Dimanche, deputy governor of Preah Sihanouk Province, told media.
The ship is scheduled to refuel before leaving ‌Cambodia on ⁠Saturday, he added.
An executive with the company, Mikael Petterson, declined to provide additional details in an email to NBC News. In a release this year announcing the company’s second residential cruise ship, Petterson said The Odyssey was 85% sold.
The company said in Tuesday’s release that it had taken significant measures to reduce fuel consumption but that those steps had failed to offset the spike in costs.
Global oil prices have surged since the war with Iran began this year, disrupting the world’s flow of fuel. In recent days, oil prices have climbed to their highest levels in months.
“Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution,” the company said. “Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees while we work toward restructuring and recapitalization over the next 60 days. That work is ongoing, and no outcome is assured.”
Randy Cassingham, a resident on the boat, wrote in a blog post that he learned his journey was over after a company official posted a note on a message board for the ship shortly after 7 a.m. Monday.
The Odyssey was entering a “temporary lay up” period — indicating it would no longer be used — and everyone had to disembark by 2 p.m., the message said, according to Cassingham, who runs ResidentialCruising.com and didn’t immediately reply to an interview request.
Cassingham attributed the development to a “cascade of problems” that he would detail later.
Pamela Reckamp, who rented a cabin with her husband and disembarked this month, said in an interview that she wasn’t surprised that the ship’s journey was over.
Reckamp, 59, recalled having attended a meeting in early September at which a company official asked cabin owners to help them raise $1 million so they could leave Ha Long Bay, Vietnam.
“She said, ‘If we don’t get this money, we have about four days of the ship running,’” Reckamp recalled. “‘Then the lights will go off and the AC will go off.’”
When the ship’s financial issues were raised during another meeting a few weeks later, Reckamp recalled, a woman stood up and said she’d bought a cabin in August and hadn’t been made aware of the issues.
“I sold my house,” Reckamp recalled the woman saying. “I sold my car. I bought my home on this ship.”
Reckamp said she felt terrible for the residents and the staff, who she said were lovely.
“We dodged a bullet,” she added.
Villa Vie Residences didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday night.
In a lawsuit filed last year, a company that bought a cabin on The Odyssey for $469,000 accused Villa Vie Residences of fraud, alleging it misrepresented its financial stability.
The company’s business model was not financially sound, the suit alleges, “but rather precarious.”
The plaintiffs are asking for a jury trial and unspecified damages of more than $100,000. Villa Vie Residences denied the allegations in the suit, which is ongoing.
Other cabins on the ship were available for significantly less money. Even though 85% of the ship was sold, the company said in 2024, prospective residents could still “secure their dream home starting at just $119,000.”
“When we launched Odyssey, we set out to prove that residential cruising wasn’t just possible — it was sustainable,” Petterson said in July.
Tim Stelloh is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.

articles.content_orig:
President of Castilla-La Mancha region says numbers likely to rise after crash in Toledo
The president of Castilla-La Mancha region, Emiliano García-Page, is now briefing the reporters.
He confirms the latest figure of 30 dead – 24 in the AVE train and six in the Iryo train – but says the authorities expect this number to rise further as emergency services are yet to reach the most affected parts of the wreckage.
He also says some 80 people were injured, with 30 people with minor injuries, and 50 with moderate and more serious injuries of varying severity.
He thanks all emergency services for their help.

He also says some 80 people were injured, with 30 people with minor injuries, and 50 with moderate and more serious injuries of varying severity.
He thanks all emergency services for their help.
Unlike other party leaders, the far-right Vox party’s Santiago Abascal appears to be going ahead with his political plans for today as he continues campaigning ahead of next month’s parliamentary election in Spain .
In his comments, he repeatedly attacked Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez for “constantly putting the Spanish people at risk.”
He explici tly rejected calls to suspend the campaign , insisting that would only to “exploit the grief and mourning to silence complaints and protests regarding the decay of our infrastructure.”
Spanish King Felipe VI appeared in front of cameras on his visit to Bétera, where he is attending some military exercises.
His brief reaction was largely in line with his earlier written statement.
Visibly shaken, Felipe VI said he wanted to “express my deep regret over this horrific incident,” acknowledging “a high number of fatalities and many injuries.”
“My primary concern is to express my sorrow over this terrible tragedy and to convey our condolences, sadness, support, and affection to the families during such an incredibly difficult and painful time.”
He also thanked emergency services responding to the incident for their help.
Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha region, has just appeared on RTVE again, confirming at least 30 dead, and saying the number may rise even further.
Local government spokesperson Padilla said the focus at the moment is on ensuring all affected get the medical help they need.
Most people are being transferred to a hospital in Toledro, but three other hospitals were also put on high readiness to support the emergency respond when needed, she said.
Another passenger on one of the trains reported that their Renfe AVE train came to a brief stop and was held up for a few minutes shortly before the crash, with the explanation given being “heavy traffic in the area.”
After it moved off again, it collided at speed with the other train, causing a “violent impact” on the passengers.
Talking to RTVE, Fernando Seco said passengers in his carriage – at the back of the train – were able to get out of the train and down the embankment, when they realised the scale of the disaster and damage to front carriages.
He said there had been no sign that anything was wrong with the train beforehand.
Miguel, ‌a passenger travelling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident.
“We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were ‌about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train – I imagine it must have been ​the other one.”
His comments were relayed by Reuters.
Castilla-la Mancha regional government said the death toll had risen to 30 from 10, in line with their previous warnings that the number could rise ( 10:46 ).
This also is in line with earlier media reports ( 11:29 ).
Early indications suggest that a Renfe AVE train from Madrid to Sevilla – the larger of the two ( 11:00 ) – collided with the Iryo train ahead of it.
Spanish news agency EFE reported that at least three carriages derailed, with some falling off the embankment, fuelling concerns that the death toll could still rise further.
The investigation will look into what caused the incident and look at both the driver’s reactions and the operation of the signalling system.
The incident took place in the Urda area of Toledro province.
The Spanish royal household has just issued their statement too, expressing their concern and support for all affected.
“We are moved and concerned by the train accident in Urda (Toledo). We share in the sorrow of the families and loved ones of the deceased and send our affection to the injured and those affected.
Our support also goes to the emergency teams and all those working in the area to help as much as possible under these circumstances.”
The emergency service of the Castilla-La Mancha government set up a hotline for all affected by the crash: 900 122 112.
Both affected train companies also set up their hotlines:
Iryo: 900 001 403 RENFE: 900 101 020
European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen responded to the train crash in Spain.
“Just received the devastating news from Toledo on the collision of two high-speed trains. My heart goes out to the victims’ families and loved ones.
Today, Europe mourns with you.”
Madrid’s blood bank has issued an “urgent appeal for blood donations” given “possible increase in unforeseen healthcare needs” for all blood groups.
Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE is reporting at least 30 dead, quoting government sources.
This has not been at this stage formally confirmed by the authorities.

Bond yields moved higher early Wednesday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's latest monetary policy decision, due later in the session.
The 10-year Treasury note yield — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was more than 2 basis points higher at 5.0134%.
The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, was up 1 basis point at 4.7494%.
Meanwhile, the yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys — which tend to move on geopolitical events — was also up by more than 1 basis point at 5.3200%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
The moves come as traders price in a 90.6% chance that the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee will leave interest rates unchanged at 375-400 basis points, according to the CME FedWatch Tool .
Investors will be closely watching Fed chairman Kevin Warsh's statement following the decision for signals on future monetary policy projections. Expectations for a 25 basis points hike at the Fed's next meeting on Dec. 9 currently stand at 76.5%.
More economic data is due Thursday. Personal consumption expenditures index — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — as well as the quarterly GDP growth rate and personal income and spending data will offer investors additional insights into the domestic economy and inflation picture.

articles.title_orig: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
articles.title_zh: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
articles.content_orig:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell , Broccoli2Shell , and HTTP2Shell .
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497 , this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update , warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
"Google Brotli contains an unchecked return value vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream," it said.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise."
While CISA's BOD 26-04 applies only to federal agencies, the cybersecurity agency urged all network defenders to prioritize patching this security flaw to block incoming attacks.
Security teams that can't apply the updates immediately should block incoming Brotli-compressed requests at the proxy or firewall level, or disable the Brotli decoding feature until they can update.
After patching, administrators must also restart affected processes and rebuild and redeploy affected container images.
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title_orig: Phantom Blade Zero Gets a 5 GB Day One Patch That Improves Ray Tracing Performance, but S-Game Warns Against New NVIDIA Drivers
articles.title_zh: Phantom Blade Zero Gets a 5 GB Day One Patch That Improves Ray Tracing Performance, but S-Game Warns Against New NVIDIA Drivers
articles.content_orig:
Chinese developer S-Game is about to release Phantom Blade Zero on PC and PlayStation 5 worldwide, and action game fans are in for something truly stunning, as Soul's adventure to save his life is so engaging that I couldn't do anything but award it a perfect score . The game is also a stunner, and thanks to a day-one patch confirmed by the game's director and producer, Soulframe Liang , the game's ray tracing and path tracing performance will be improved.
"We rushed to prepare a day-one patch before launch, approximately 5 GB in size," wrote Soulframe in a heartfelt message shared on Chinese social media and translated on the Phantom Blade Zero subreddit . "It can significantly improve ray-tracing and path-tracing performance, as well as fix some bugs. If you have already preloaded the game, you can download this additional update before launching it. If you haven't preloaded the game, downloading it directly will give you the latest version."
As I highlighted in my review, I played Phantom Blade Zero with ray tracing disabled, as it was surprisingly demanding and would have forced me to use NVIDIA DLSS in Performance Mode to achieve the baseline 60 FPS needed to have a good experience with Frame Generation , so this is definitely good news, although the game looks stunning even without it.
Speaking about performance, Soulframe Liang also issued a warning for all those planning to play Phantom Blade Zero on an NVIDIA GPU . "We discovered that NVIDIA's latest 621.01 driver exhibits unstable performance in certain situations," Soulframe wrote. "After testing, we found that driver version 617.42 currently provides the best compatibility with Phantom Blade Zero. If you've already updated to a version newer than 617.42, you can select the corresponding older version from NVIDIA's recent driver releases and perform a clean reinstall. Alternatively, you can wait for NVIDIA's next driver update, which we believe will be released soon."
Having not updated my RTX 4080 driver to version 621.01 , I cannot say how much of an impact it has on performance, but on driver 617.14 I experienced little to no issues, so until a new driver is released, it would be best to follow Soulframe Liang's advice. Hopefully, all players will have an experience as technically flawless as I had, as Phantom Blade Zero deserves to be enjoyed at its best.
About the author : Francesco De Meo has been covering video games and technology since 2012, starting his career at small outlets like Gamersyndrome and GeekSnack. 

After joining Wccftech gaming section in 2015, he quickly expanded his video gaming coverage with in-depth reporting, interviews with iconic industry figures such as Grasshopper Manufacture founder and No More Heroes creator Goichi "Suda51" Suda, Resident Evil series creator Shinji Mikami, Team NINJA's president and Nioh series director Fumihiko Yasuda, and Silent Hill creator Keiichiro Toyama, reviews and on-the-ground coverage of major industry events such as Gamescom and E3.

When he's not reporting or reviewing, Francesco can be found playing the genres he loves most, spending time with his six cats, reading, writing music, playing guitar and drumming for his progressive rock band.

articles.content_orig:
Warhammer Age of Sigmar: October Update
New rules updates are going live for Warhammer Age of Sigmar – read on to see if they affect your army.
Major changes: Khazalite Holds, Sons of Behemat
Minor changes: Ogor Mawtribes, Lumineth Realm-lords, Skaven, Sylvaneth, Nighthaunt
With the advent of new battletomes, a few older rules needed a quick update to stay relevant – namely where keywords were involved. The Khazalite Holds in particular see a lot of older FYRESLAYERS keywords turned into the new GRIMMDRON ,* so things like the Fyreslayers Scourge of Aqshy rules can still be used.
As well as having their keywords changed, the Lofnir Drothkeepers Army of Renown has also been rewritten slightly to better fit their new rules. Notably, it now includes an additional way to generate grudge marks when your Magmadroths are killed.
The Sons of Behemat previously struggled to field game-legal 2,000 point Armies of Renown without needing to dip into Auxiliaries, so now they have a new option to field regiments led by Mancrusher Gargants.** This applies for both the Matriarch’s Mob and Stomper Tribe , so now’s a great time to give their new options a go.
Besides these two larger updates, a few fixes and clarifications have been added to several factions, such as the Skaven’s Verminlord Corruptor having its points corrected after a typo in the last update – one that most of you caught onto anyway, but a slip-up nonetheless! Some units like Pyregheists and Ydrilan Riverblades can also now double up their Champions when reinforced, like other, similar warscrolls. If your faction of choice is listed under minor changes , have a quick look for their updates with the New tag (or search for the ✹ icon).
Minor changes: Daughters of Khaine Heartflayer Troupe, Nighthaunt Slasher Host, Orruk Warclans Swampskulka Gang, Seraphon Sunblood Prowlers
This is one of the largest Spearhead updates we’ve had for a while, with a handful of ability clarifications that add the ‘Once Per Turn (Army)’ condition to bring them in line with other factions. Otherwise, it’s business as usual in the Spearhead arena, so get out into the City of Ash and show those scuttling Skaven miscreants what for.
Download the latest changes, enjoy your battles in the Mortal Realms, and if you have anything you need answered, make sure to send your questions to AoSFAQ@gwplc.com .

articles.title_orig: China’s Electric Carmakers Are Running Out of Domestic Buyers | The 10-Point for Oct. 28
articles.title_zh: China’s Electric Carmakers Are Running Out of Domestic Buyers | The 10-Point for Oct. 28
articles.content_orig:
To understand why China is desperate to ship cars overseas, visit a dealership in Beijing.
Autumn has traditionally been the peak time to buy vehicles in the country, but this year many showrooms are empty or shut.
Car salesman Li Ke said that other than the Covid-19 pandemic, the 2026 "golden September and silver October" season, as it's known, is the slowest he's seen in his 26 years on the job.
"In past years, customers would come to the showrooms nonstop," he told CNBC during an interview in his deserted showroom at a complex of dealerships on the outskirts of the Chinese capital. "We would have deals to sign every day. But nowadays we see only two to three deals a week. It's a dramatic drop."
Many people in China aren't buying cars because an unstable job market and a continued slide in property prices have undercut consumer confidence. The government has also scaled back incentives such as cash-for-clunkers subsidies and tax breaks to go electric, car salespeople said.
Passenger car retail sales for 2026 in China totaled 13.33 million units through September, falling 21.7% from a year ago, according to the China Passenger Car Association. For the full year 2026, China's domestic passenger car retail sales are set to drop 22% to 18.5 million vehicles, the association said — under the level recorded in the first year of the pandemic.
Even electric vehicles, which were once a bright spot, are down. Gasoline car sales have been declining in China because of the country's transition to electric vehicles, but sales in China of new-energy vehicles — which includes EVs — dropped by 12.8% from January through September, according to the association.
"Customers are watching every penny," Li said. "When looking at all the new functions on all these new models, they are weighing what is most practical, economic and worth their money over the long term. We don't see impulse buying. Because of the bad economy, people are taking more time to replace their cars."
The fierce competition has led to bruising price wars in recent years, a key reason Chinese carmakers have cast their eyes overseas and why Beijing is fearful of partners like the U.S. and Europe putting up coordinated trade barriers against its massive car exports, analysts said.
Industrial profits for the first nine months of the year were up 15.5% from the same period in 2025, but September showed signs of weakness relative to the prior eight months, according to China's National Bureau of Statistics . For the auto manufacturing industry specifically, profits from January to September shrank by 22.8% compared with last year.
To preserve cash, Li's dealership moved out of a pricey streetside space to one with less foot traffic but that rents at a fraction of the cost.
With profit margins eroding, Li said he sees little point in offering further discounts. He said the bigger hurdle is the prevailing Chinese consumer attitude toward big-ticket purchases.
"Chinese buyers would rather wait," he said.
